# Phase M3.3: highest-yield source acquisition plan (audit only)

*Generated by `tools/m33-source-plan.py --report` from `data/audit/m3.3-source-acquisition-plan.jsonl`; do not edit by hand. Nothing was fetched, crawled, OCR'd or written to the model; the score ranks sources, it establishes no fact.*

## If there is one short session for new-data acquisition

**Acquire first: mission-haut-brion.com** (B · first-party URL seen, never fetched): 12 document-less vintage(s) of Château La Mission Haut-Brion, none of them reachable from a held document, through 55 already-discovered first-party URL(s) naming those vintages; effort M. At most **12 items** could resolve (confidence: 12 medium) - only after the fetch and an evidence review of each document.

But the larger yield needs no acquisition at all: **182 document-less vintages already have a document the evidence store accepted for exactly that wine and vintage**, unlinked in the model, and 140 more have a fetched estate document headed with the year. Mapping those (category A) comes before any fetch.

## 2. Methodology

- **Items.** A register gap is an estate's whole set of document-less vintages, or one figure group; the items are what resolve one by one, so candidates are scored on items and also report the gap ids they touch.
- **Existing corpus first.** For every item the evidence is sought in this order: an accepted evidence decision for exactly that wine and vintage not linked in the model (A); a fetched document of the estate headed with the year (A); a first-party URL the crawl saw and never fetched (B); a first-party link that redirected off-site (B); blocked (E) or dead (B, unavailable) URLs, recorded, never ranked; nothing known (D).
- **Confidence.** A, accepted: HIGH. A, fetched: MEDIUM when the wine's name is in the title or address, else LOW (it may be another wine of the estate). B: HIGH when the address names the year, the wine and is a sheet (PDF or sheet word); MEDIUM with the year and one of those; LOW with the year alone.
- **Score** (deterministic, documented in `score()`): 3 per HIGH item, 2 per MEDIUM, 1 per LOW; +3 first-party, +3 already discovered, +4 already stored, +3 three or more vintages, +2 two or more wines, +2 provenance tied to the exact document; -2 OCR, -3 broad crawling, -4 third-party only; divided by the effort midpoint (XS 0.25, S 0.75, M 2.5, L 10, XL 20, UNKNOWN 20). Effort is the acquisition effort, or for held documents the mapping effort. Blocked, dead, decision-blocked and discovery-only candidates score 0 and are listed apart.
- **Effort.** Fetch: XS up to 5 URLs, S 25, M 120, L 500, XL more (one polite request per URL, robots delay 1.5 s, then an evidence review per document). Mapping held documents: XS up to 10 items, S 60, M 300, L more.
- **Order:** score, then high-confidence gaps, then effort, then id.

## 10. Unresolved limitations

- **Most document-less vintages have no known source.** 1,041 of 1,403 have nothing known to hold them, and 1,256 of the 1,403 are in the model only through a critic rating, with no sheet: the estates may never have published one online. Finding one is discovery (D), not acquisition.
- **The URL match is lexical.** A year and a wine name in an address suggest the document; only fetching and reading it establishes what it holds.
- **Fetched-document matches (A, MEDIUM/LOW) may concern another wine** of the estate (a second wine's sheet headed with the same year); each needs review.
- **The crawl state is a snapshot** (2026-10-25): a skipped URL may have moved or gone since.
- **Policy stands.** URLs refused by robots.txt or an AI-agent rule are never acquired, even when they name the exact document.
